questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest driving speed?

options.text: The speed of the traffic around you.
Much slower than the surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as nearby vehicles. When all vehicles move at the same speed in the same direction, collisions are less likely. But never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Is driving at night safer or more dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see hazards, headlight glare can hurt your vision, and there are more tired and impaired drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: Which of these is okay to find during a pre-trip tire inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 2/32 inch in the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. All tires should be the same size, not cracked, have the right air pressure, and not be worn too much. Tires from different makers are acceptable.

questions.question: What might you be asked to do during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back into an alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include these maneuvers: straight line backing, offset back parking (right and left), driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Why should charter bus passengers not board until departure time?

options.text: The bus costs money from when the first passenger boards, so boarding late saves money.
Passengers will get on and off multiple times, and might miss the departure.
Passengers should not pick their seats before the bus is about to leave.
Waiting to load helps prevent theft and damage to the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting to load helps prevent theft and damage to the bus.
questions.explanation: Drivers should wait until departure time to board passengers. This helps prevent theft and vandalism on the bus.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will move out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: Act quickly if your brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will be moving, and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: How often should you stop to take a break while driving to avoid fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours.
questions.explanation: On a long drive, take a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles to avoid becoming too tired.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right when rain starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road but has not yet washed away. This creates a very slippery surface.

questions.question: What should you do with access panels before driving?

options.text: Store them in the storage compartment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close them.
questions.explanation: Before driving, do an outside inspection of your bus. Make sure all emergency exits and access panels are closed.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle improperly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You get an extra point against your final score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, always face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If driving a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you automatically fail the test.

questions.question: A fatigued driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter remedies to stay awake.
May make important decisions too slowly.
Is usually more careful than a typical driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: When you are fatigued, you will not see or react to hazards as quickly. Your ability to make important decisions will be impaired.

questions.question: If you are transporting a drunk passenger, you should:

options.text: Force them to exit the bus immediately.
Wait until you reach a safe area, like a stop or well-lit place, before asking them to exit.
Give them coffee to help them sober up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you reach a safe area, like a stop or well-lit place, before asking them to exit.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for a drunk passenger's safety. Have them exit at a safe location, such as the next scheduled stop or a well-lit area where other people are present.

questions.question: Distracted drivers may be:

options.text: Focused on using their cell phones.
Not talking to anyone in their vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Focused on using their cell phones.
questions.explanation: You can tell another driver is distracted if they drift between lanes, drive at changing speeds, use a cell phone, look at a map, eat, or talk with passengers.

questions.question: The best way to avoid glare from oncoming vehicles at night is to:

options.text: Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, look toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: If a bus has a brake and accelerator interlock system, the system should:

options.text: Be turned off in most situations.
Only be used in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never replace the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Some buses have a brake and accelerator interlock system that applies the brakes when the rear door is open. This system should not be used instead of the parking brake.

questions.question: If equipped, a header board should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a header board, make sure it is secure, undamaged, and strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: Drivers behind a slow-moving vehicle often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow too closely.
questions.explanation: It is common for drivers to tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive safely.
questions.explanation: To reduce aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. Drive at a safe speed.

questions.question: Bridges usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be extra careful on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Yawning repeatedly or rubbing your eyes

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting a shoulder rumble strip, or feeling restless and irritable.
